dedupe_keys.name: us forest service wood tornado shelter design and impact test results

description: The Forest Service Forest Products Laboratory project page for a tornado shelter built from small-diameter timber, with the design assumptions and test results behind it. Researchers led by Robert H. Falk used an air-pressurised debris launcher to follow FEMA standards: a 15 lb No. 2 Southern Pine 2 by 4 in. missile fired at 100 mph at a safe room wall to simulate tornado debris, and a 9 lb missile at 34 mph for hurricane debris. Walls of four-ply laminated logs needed extra buffering; laminated logs reinforced with tempered or composite hardboard on the inside gave improved results. The page follows FEMA 320, FEMA 361 and the National Performance Criteria for Tornado Shelters, and extends earlier work at the Wind Engineering Research Center at Texas Tech University. Contents: eight step-by-step construction guides, construction drawings, wind pressure test papers for components (2016) and a wood tornado safe room door design paper (2016). Coverage: the United States. Access: free web page; the page shows it was last updated on 19 August 2026. Licence: not stated. Caveats: the results are for one shelter design. Useful as fragility and design evidence for storm wind resilience of small buildings; related records are not yet linked.
